newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks in 5th straight record on data.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks in 5th straight record on data.

text.p: Mexican shares pared earlier gains due to a late slide on Wall Street, but still ended up and posted their fifth record close in a row. Analysts and dealers said foreign fund flows resumed after an announcement of strong industrial output data.
"Industrial activity data are a positive, and the market is in a positive-positive frame of mind," said Felix Boni, head of research at ING-Barings Mexico.
Final closing prices showed the blue chip IPC share index gained 16.99 points on the day, or 0.40 percent, to a new record of 4,276.83.
"The prepayment is part of the same tonic we have seen, of money flowing into Mexico," Boni added.

"Funds are flowing in because Mexico has lagged compared to Latin America this year and due to reduced fears over the forthcoming elections," he said, referring to mid-term elections to be held on July 6.
Dealers all said they had seen heavy buying by foreign investors.
"The bourse gathered pace after the industrial output data were released. There were droves of foreign buyers, particularly for financials," a floor trader said.
"Buyers seem to consider financials to be cheap," the trader added.
"Financials were very cheap...they are a leveraged way for foreign investors to play the Mexican recovery," said Enrique Pani, an analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell-Mexico.
Bancomer, one of Mexico's biggest financial groups, chalked up strong gains. The B class share rose 13 centavos to 3.93 pesos, while the A class ended up 5 centavos at 2.10 pesos.
The two share series accounted for more than one-quarter of all shares traded during the session.

Dealers said Telmex weighed down most on the market and ended off two centavos at 18.70 pesos, due to the downdraft from Wall Street rather than any fundamental reason. The telecomms stock's ADRs closed down 1/4 to 47-1/8.
The Dow Jones industrial average closed down 11.31 points at 7,760.78.

Dealers also drew attention to gains by retail chain Controladora Comercial Mexicana, up 10 centavos to 6.96 pesos. Dealers said there was appreciable trade in the stock, although two hefty cross trades accounted for most of its volume.
Traders said the firm had lagged behind its sector counterpart Cifra. One dealer said heavy deals were due to speculation on a possible sale by Comercial Mexicana of its restaurant holdings.
On the broad market, 122 stocks in total traded, of which gainers outpaced sliders by 56 to 38.
Banorte, a financial stock not included in the IPC, was the most heavily traded of the prominent gainers .PG.MX after climbing 40 centavos to 8.56 pesos.
